newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen A shares drag B shares to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen A shares drag B shares to lower close.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index closed down on Monday because of downward pressure from falls in the domestic A share market , brokers said.
The B share index shed 1.23 points or 0.94 percent to 130.03 points on thin turnover of HK$33 million against HK$31 million last Friday.
The yuan-denominated A share index tumbled 13.66 points or 3.35 percent to 394.46 points, with turnover contracting to 5.0 billion yuan from 5.8 billion in the previous session.
"B shares fell because of the bearishness of A shares," a broker at China Southern Securities Co said.
"Investors did not actively participate in trading due to a lack of confidence," the broker said.

Brokers said A shares were depressed in the absence of powerful players such as state banks and listed firms after Beijing in May banned them from speculative share trading amid a string of crackdown measures aimed at cooling the over-heated bourses.
Falls in market leader Shenzhen Development Bank also had a strong negative impact on the overall market, they said.
The bank slid 1.29 yuan to 33.58 yuan on heavy volume of 8.6 million shares valued at 293 million yuan.
Shares of the bank had entered a downward cycle after the company last week forecast slower earnings growth for 1997, brokers said.
The bank is a major factor on the Shenzhen stock market because of its large market capitalisation and its position as mainland China's only listed bank.
Crystal display maker Tianma Microelectronics was the worst A share performer, diving 2.25 yuan to its 10 percent limit-down at 20.22 yuan.
Shenzhen Yantian Harbour Co Ltd, which listed 116 million A shares on Monday, was the most actively traded on heavy volum e of 75 million shares.
The counter opened at 12.19 yuan and closed at 10.71 yuan, compared with the issue price of 5.31 yuan per share.
The firm operates port facilities in Shenzhen's Yantian Harbour, northeast of Hong Kong.
The company's biggest shareholder, Yantian Harbour Group, has a 27 percent stake in a HK$3 billion marine container handling venture, Yantian International, with Hutchison Whampoa Ltd.
On the B share market, conglomerate Shenzhen Zhonghao (Group) Co Ltd was the biggest loser, sliding HK$0.26, its daily maximum of 10 percent, to HK$2.32 on thin volume of 15,500 shares.

Shares of Bengang Steel Plates was the most actively traded on Monday on volume of 2.3 million shares, dipping HK$0.07 to HK$2.03. The newcomer has benn moving below its offer price of HK$2.38 per share since its debut earlier this month.
